title: Plural sarve address in Ramayana 7.45.2
predecessor_review: PG887 constructed the ordinary freestanding sarva M vocative-plural key. PG890 directly attested only M vocative singular. No PG887 position, reading or ending history is recredited here.

source_request.sense: all members of the seated addressed group
source_request.verbal_pada: P for srnuta; A for kurudhvam

semantic_interfaces.role: honorific continuation of the addressed group

syntax_interfaces.role: plural addressee plus second-person plural imperative

source_policy_decisions: Admit sarve at Ramayana 7.45.2 as positive masculine-plural addressee-function evidence because it directly governs two plural imperatives and co-refers with the speech's masculine and second-person plural controls.
Retain exact formal NOM/VOC classification as Open: sarve is surface-syncretic, and the pinned witness supplies neither he nor an explicit case gloss.
Do not transfer this locus to feminine, neuter, singular, dual, accent, compound or Vedic sarva histories, and do not recredit PG887 morphology.

controls.reason: sarve is the all-member addressee expression before plural commands
NOMpl and VOCpl are syncretic and this source has no explicit case label
the governing predicates are second-person plural commands, not third-person statements
one masculine plural discourse does not attest other gender-number keys
